title: introduce-fillrate-aware-autoscaler-and-safety-probe
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently balance capacity using slot-based headroom and util signals. That approach can leave the fleet vulnerable to sustained high request rates (fill-rate) from a subset of tenants which drives up token egress and causes tail latency or throttling for other workloads. This PR adds a Fill-Rate Aware Autoscaler (FRA) and a runtime Safety Probe designed to detect sustained throttle pressure and take graceful, observable remediation actions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Introduces a new controller that computes per-tenant fill-rate budgets (requests/sec and tokens/sec) from rolling windows, exposes a tunable smoothing policy, and integrates with the existing reservation/lease system to reserve a fraction of throughput for fairness. Adds a lightweight Safety Probe that samples queue depth, gateway-drop-rates and KV-cache miss spikes and emits a decision signal (throttle-shed / soft-fallback) to the request router. The system prefers non-disruptive mitigations first (probe-triggered slow-path routing, prefix-cache priority adjustments, temporary soft-quota annotations) and escalates to short-lived request shedding only when pressure persists beyond a hysteresis window.

Design notes and decisions: - Fill-rate budget is computed per-tenant using a 5m rolling window and p95 throughput target; budget decays with an exponential factor to handle bursty workloads. - Budget enforcement is opportunistic: we attempt to honor budgets by steering requests to warm pools or lower-cost model variants before applying hard throttles. - Safety Probe samples are aggregated across pools; the probe publishes a single severity label per tenant that downstream request routers consult. - All control actions are recorded in a new event stream (event:fillrate-control) to preserve traceability and to feed Optimize/Console. - Feature gated behind "fillrate_autoscaler_v1"; off by default for Dedicated clusters.

Checklist: - [x] Controller and allocator changes implemented - [x] Unit tests for budget computation and smoothing - [x] E2E integration harness run in staging against synthetic tenants - [x] Prometheus metrics added and dashboard template drafted - [x] Migration/rollout plan documented - [x] Docs: design doc and operator notes added

Commits summary: - feat(autoscaler): new fillrate controller, budget calculator, smoothing policy - feat(allocator): reserve-throughput hook into lease allocator - feat(runtime): safety-probe sampler and router hooks - docs(design): fillrate-autoscaler design + operator runbook - test: integration harness scenarios for noisy-tenant and steady-state - ci: add e2e gate and new lint exceptions for generated protobufs

Files changed (high-level): - controllers/autoscaler/fillrate_controller.go - internal/allocator/fill_budget.go - runtime/probe/fillrate_probe.go - runtime/router/fillrate_hook.go - deployments/helm/values-dedicated.yaml (feature gate + defaults) - docs/design/fillrate-autoscaler.md - test/e2e/fillrate_noisy_tenant_test.go - pkg/metrics/metrics_prometheus.go (new metrics and labels)

Metrics and observability: New Prometheus metrics introduced: - redwood_fillrate_budget{tenant,window} gauge - redwood_fillrate_usage{tenant,window} gauge - redwood_fillrate_probe_severity{tenant} gauge (0=ok,1=warn,2=critical) - redwood_fillrate_shed_count counter - redwood_fillrate_shed_duration_seconds histogram Dashboards: added staging dashboard under console/dashboards/fillrate-autoscaler.json (template). Traceability: all control signals emit events routed to the eventstore (event.type=fillrate-control).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; default off. 2) Canary on internal staging Dedicated cluster with 3 tenants for 48h. 3) Gradual enable for 5% customer Dedicated fleets for 72h with extra alerting. 4) Monitor token egress, p95 latency, and redwood_fillrate_probe_severity; rollback if probe_severity>1 sustained > 30m.

Backward compatibility and safety: The FRA hooks are additive; when the feature is disabled the allocator and router behavior is unchanged. All external APIs and annotations are opt-in. We keep the old headroom autopilot in place as a fallback.

Migration/Maintenance notes for operators: - Helm values keys: dedicated.fillrate.enabled, dedicated.fillrate.reserve_fraction, dedicated.fillrate.window_seconds - When enabling, ensure eventstore retention is at least 7d to inspect control history. - If noisy tenant is misclassified, operator can set annotation idle:fillrate-bypass=true to temporarily opt-out a tenant from enforcement.

Testing performed: Unit tests cover budget math and smoothing; integration tests simulate noisy tenants and verify fallback routing; manual run in staging confirmed metrics and graceful degradation paths. CI: build+unit+lint passed, e2e initially flaky on a timeout in staging (re-run fixed the flaky test).

Breaking change: none.

review_thread: Ethan Moore (review): Can we avoid cross-pool global locks when computing global usage? Suggest we use a best-effort aggregator with eventual consistency.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Answered - aggregator is sharded per-pool and we publish summarized usage to avoid global locks; added comments and a sharding test.
Lina Zhou (review): The smoothing hyperparams look sensitive; can you expose them via Helm and add defaults that match fleet size?
Aisha Kapoor (author): Exposed dedicated.fillrate.smoothing_alpha and provided reasonable defaults in values-dedicated.yaml; added unit tests that assert stability across alpha range.
Carlos Mendes (review): Concern: event noise in Optimize/Console. Please ensure we sample or throttle event emission.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Implemented event coalescing (1s window) and a sampling limiter; updated docs to describe event stream cost.
Lina Zhou (approval): Approving after hyperparam exposure and docs updates.
Ethan Moore (approval): Approving after sharding tests and comment cleanup.
CI: e2e flaky test failed first run, second run passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Add a feature-gated Fill-Rate Aware Autoscaler and runtime Safety Probe to manage sustained request-rate pressure on Dedicated fleets. Operators must enable via helm: dedicated.fillrate.enabled=true. Includes metrics and dashboards.
